A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FedDUAL work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are accessible, allowing retained, relocated and newly added material to be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification experiments on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100 and FMNIST, alongside component ablations, learning curves and heterogeneity analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds CIFAR component ablations, another gradient diagnostic and runtime measurements.

M1.justification: Both versions use the same accuracy-gap-dependent sigmoid coefficient, cross-entropy/KL adaptive loss, final-layer Wasserstein aggregation and averaging of earlier layers. Algorithm 1 retains the same procedure. Expanded explanations and revised appendix derivations do not establish an implemented method change.

E1.justification: Coverage remains CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100 and FMNIST image classification, with IID/non-IID diagnostics and label-heterogeneity experiments. The additional ablations and timing measurements use these existing benchmarks without introducing another task, domain or population.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains FedAvg, FedProx, FedNova, FedBN, FedDyn, MOON, SCAFFOLD and FedPVR. The component-ablation configurations are also retained, and the new runtime comparisons reuse existing baselines.

E3.justification: The principal accuracy protocol remains unchanged. New runtime evaluations introduce client/server timing, fixed-budget comparisons over 80 CIFAR-10 rounds and 180 FMNIST rounds, and time-to-target measurements at 40% and 70% accuracy, respectively.

E4.justification: v2 substantially expands supporting analysis through CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100 component ablations, a CIFAR-10/VGG16 gradient-norm diagnostic in Figure 2, and computational-cost and runtime analyses in Appendices C–D. Existing FMNIST layer, hyperparameter and heterogeneity analyses are retained; moving their discussion into the main text is not new evidence.

E5.justification: v2 adds uncertainty bands to benchmark learning curves in Figure 10. Both versions already report three runs with different seeds and mean-plus-standard-deviation accuracy values; no increased run count is documented. The new figure does not clearly specify what its bands represent.

E6.justification: Table 1 and the original FMNIST ablation values are unchanged. Table 2 adds CIFAR component results, including adaptive-loss-only accuracies of 41.05% and 25.05% on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100. Tables 3–5 add client/server, fixed-budget and target-accuracy timings, substantially extending the reported outcomes rather than demonstrating an improvement over v1's headline accuracy.

T1.justification: v1's short convergence arguments under two assumptions are replaced by six assumptions, modified-loss lemmas and detailed convex/non-convex derivations. v2 changes the stated convex bound from O(1/sqrt(T)) to O(1/T) plus a constant and introduces explicit Wasserstein approximation terms. Appendix C also adds formal computational-complexity analysis.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same central claims: a dual adaptive-loss/aggregation method, improved performance and convergence under heterogeneity, evaluation on three datasets against eight baselines, and convex/non-convex guarantees. The abstract's added references to gradient instability and sharp minima restate existing motivation.

C2.justification: v2 revises the explanation of beta, adds justification for parameter-distribution KL regularization, interprets adaptive-loss-only underperformance, and develops runtime tradeoffs and prospective differential-privacy integration. It also reverses the stated alpha–accuracy trend despite retaining the heterogeneity plot, introducing an inconsistent interpretation.

D1.justification: Appendices C–D newly provide model parameter-count estimates, computational breakdowns and measured training times. The principal hardware, software, optimizer, hyperparameter-search and code-access disclosures remain unchanged. These additions document the implementation and costs without establishing a changed implementation.

R1.justification: The main related-work section is retained. v2 removes the Yu et al. (2019) reference and adds explicit theoretical positioning against FedAvg, FedProx and SCAFFOLD in Appendix B.2, plus discussion contrasting parameter-distribution KL with other alignment approaches.

P1.justification: v2 substantially reorganizes the exposition: it inserts a Definitions section, expands method explanations, moves hyperparameter and heterogeneity discussions into the main ablation section, and relocates and expands limitations in the appendix. The convergence appendix is extensively rewritten and reorganized.

P2.justification: v2 expands Figure 2 into two panels, restructures Table 2 by dataset, adds three runtime tables and introduces the uncertainty-curve Figure 10. Figure 5 and the ablation table also receive different placements and layouts. Existing plot images are otherwise retained, including the renumbered appendix plots.

improvement.justification: The additional ablations, uncertainty curves and runtime measurements improve empirical transparency. However, the new 35% server-overhead argument conflicts with Table 3: CIFAR-10 server times are 1.94 versus 0.44 seconds, and FMNIST times are 1.95 versus 0.05. The revised non-convex derivation drops the approximation term's 1/eta factor after Equation 85, and the heterogeneity prose contradicts the retained plot. These substantive problems in the new efficiency and convergence justification make the net quality effect uncertain.
